ai.summary: Removed NODE_AUTH_TOKEN environment variable from publish step in .github/workflows/sdk-release.yml. Workflow now relies on Trusted Publisher auth configured in npm site. Affects sdk-release CI only.

eli5.text: The automated process that publishes new versions of the software development kit (SDK) has stopped using a stored password-like secret to log into the package registry. Instead, it now relies on a newer, more secure method called Trusted Publishing, which is set up directly through the npm website. This change only affects the internal release pipeline itself; nobody using the SDK needs to take any action, and the published packages remain exactly the same.

ai.title: Codebuff CLI 1.0.614 ships /subscribe and free-mode credit bypass
ai.summary: Version 1.0.614 of the codebuff CLI rolls up same-day changes from the main branch into a single release. The /subscribe command replaces /buy-credits in the CLI command registry and now opens a dedicated web subscribe page instead of /pricing or /profile. Free mode chat completions now bypass credit depletion checks so free agent/model combinations remain accessible even when user credit balance is zero or subscription quotas exhausted. The release also removes NODE_AUTH_TOKEN from the sdk-release workflow in favor of Trusted Publisher auth and softens speed claims in web documentation with specific eval data.
ai.evidence: In cli/release/package.json, the version field of the codebuff package changed from 1.0.613 to 1.0.614 (diff hunk @@ -1,6 +1,6 @@ shows version line update, commit authored 2026-02-07T04:40:58Z as a release-bump with +1/-1 stats).

eli5.text: Codebuff 1.0.614 delivers better free access and a simpler way to manage your account. First, the tool now stays usable even when you are out of paid credits, because free requests skip the usual credit checks so you can keep working at no cost. Second, the old "buy credits" command is now just "subscribe," and it takes you straight to a clean subscription page with the navigation chrome hidden for a focused checkout flow. The developer-facing release publishing step also quietly dropped an old secret token in favor of modern trusted-authentication, keeping the SDK release pipeline secure. Upgrading means you can keep coding with free requests uninterrupted and managing your plan is one fewer click.

eli5.text: The text people see while signing up for the service was made shorter and simpler. If you're someone walking through the signup steps now, the headings and explanations read more quickly, titles like "Get the CLI" and "Run Codebuff in your project" replaced longer phrases, and the referral code step dropped a celebratory emoji and extra wording. This only affects the web-based onboarding screens you view in a browser; nothing about how the software works behind the scenes changed.

eli5.text: When you type the old command to get a referral code, it now answers to a new name and shows you a ready-made link you can copy with one click. The referral feature itself, earning credits for inviting friends, is unchanged, but the command was renamed from the old name to the clearer new name, and your unique referral link is now displayed in a banner with a copy button instead of requiring you to build the link yourself. If you still type the old name, it works as a shortcut to the new command, so nothing breaks. This is live today for anyone using the CLI referral command.

ai.title: SDK 0.10.3 ships subscribe, refer-friends, and free-mode fixes
ai.summary: Version 0.10.3 of @codebuff/sdk rolls up same-day changes from main into a single release bump in sdk/package.json. The cycle ships the /subscribe command replacing /buy-credits, the /refer-friends slash command with copyable referral links, Node 24 in the sdk-release CI workflow, and free-mode chat completions that bypass credit depletion checks for free agent/model combinations. The release also removes NODE_AUTH_TOKEN in favor of Trusted Publisher auth and softens speed claims in web documentation with specific eval data.
ai.evidence: sdk/package.json hunk increments version from 0.10.2 to 0.10.3; analysis notes confirm "Bump SDK version to 0.10.3" with accompanying same-day commits covering /subscribe, /refer-friends, Node 24 SDK release CI, and free-mode credit bypass.

eli5.text: Codebuff 0.10.3, dated 2026-02-07, is fundamentally an SDK packaging release. The title, subtitle, and category all explicitly state this is a 'SDK' release (not a product feature drop), and the single, specific capability change listed is: the SDK package version was updated to 0.10.3. There are no new user-facing AI models, CLI slash commands, agent behaviors, authentication flows, billing adjustments, or performance enhancements included in 0.10.3 itself. The only functional change bundled within this exact version tag is the version bump of the SDK package from 0.10.2 to 0.10.3. All other listed changes were previously shipped in earlier release tags spanning January 23 to February 7, 2026, and are already included in versions preceding this release. Upgrading to SDK 0.10.3 updates your SDK package version identifier to 0.10.3 but delivers no new end-user capabilities or behaviors beyond what was already available in version 0.10.2. This is purely a versioning and packaging marker release for the SDK component.

ai.title: SDK build script hardens TypeScript declaration bundling
ai.summary: SDK build script `scripts/build.ts` now points to `tsconfig.build.json` for declaration bundling and exits with code 1 on failure instead of warning. `tsconfig.build.json` updates target to `ES2023`, lib to `ESNext`, adds `types: ["node"]`, and defines `baseUrl` and `paths` for `@codebuff` packages to ensure `index.d.ts` bundles correctly into `dist`. This fixes issues where type definitions were not being generated or bundled properly during SDK builds.

eli5.text: When you build the Codebuff SDK into a package, the tool that generates the TypeScript declaration files (index.d.ts) now uses a corrected setup that properly resolves all the internal package paths and targets modern ES2023 standards, and if declaration generation fails, the build now crashes loudly with an error code 1 instead of silently warning and continuing. This matters because the tool that assembles the bundled type definitions previously couldn't correctly trace imports across the @codebuff/* packages, which meant the published.d.ts files in dist were often incomplete or missing type information for cross-package dependencies. Previously, when declaration bundling failed during CI, the build script would print a warning and exit successfully (code 0), allowing the release to ship

ai.title: SDK ships 0.10.4
ai.summary: The `@codebuff/sdk` package is released as version 0.10.4, incrementing from 0.10.3. This release is a pure version bump committed to the `sdk` package manifest. The 0.10.4 release bundles the TypeScript declaration bundling hardening introduced in 0.10.3's follow-up build script: `scripts/build.ts` now targets `tsconfig.build.json` (ES2023 target, ESNext lib, `@codebuff` path aliases) for declaration generation and exits with code 1 on failure. As a result, the published `dist/index.d.ts` bundles internal `@codebuff/*` type references correctly, resolving missing type definitions for SDK consumers.
ai.evidence: Commit 307a6696 modifies `sdk/package.json`, changing the `@codebuff/sdk` version field from `0.10.3` to `0.10.4`, with a diff stat of +1/-1.

eli5.text: This release hardens the SDK's TypeScript declaration bundling. The build script now targets ES2023 and ESNext libraries, adds Node types, and defines base URL paths for @codebuff packages, ensuring index.d.ts bundles correctly into dist. Importantly, the build script now exits with code 1 on failure instead of just warning, which means type definition errors won't silently slip through. These changes fix issues where type definitions were not being generated or bundled properly during SDK builds, so developers get more reliable type information when using the SDK.

ai.title: Add grant-credits.ts script
ai.summary: New internal script `scripts/grant-credits.ts` enables manual credit grants via CLI. Prompts for user email/ID, amount, and description; validates inputs; displays summary; requires confirmation. Inserts record into `credit_ledger` with type `admin`, priority 50, no expiration. Uses `@codebuff/internal/db` and `drizzle-orm`.

eli5.text: Your account can now be credited directly by someone with admin tools, as if you had been given a paid balance without going through a public billing screen. A new staff command walks an internal tool through adding a specific number of credits to a user's account, recording the reason and requiring a final yes/no confirmation before saving. If you are an admin, you will see a summary on the screen that shows exactly who is getting the credits, how many, why, and that the grant never expires; for everyone else, nothing about your experience changes because this tool stays behind the staff-only console.

ai.title: CLI 1.0.615 release bundles refer-friends, ad panel, and SDK build
ai.summary: Freebuff CLI 1.0.615 is a release-bump increment over 1.0.614, packaging the same-day commits as the released version. This release cycle ships the /refer-friends slash command replacing /referral (with referral and redeem as aliases), a CLI ad-banner info panel with a disable button driven by new onDisableAds and isFreeMode props, simplified onboarding copy with emoji stripped, simplified Web buy credits panel using fixed dollar options, the grant-credits.ts admin credit script writing admin-priority rows to credit_ledger, Node 24 in the sdk-release CI workflow, and hardened SDK TypeScript declaration bundling via tsconfig.build.json. The commit itself touches only cli/release/package.json; all feature and fix changes reside in the preceding commits.
ai.evidence: Version string changed from 1.0.614 to 1.0.615 in cli/release/package.json (release-bump commit c62be772), with no other code modifications; the user-visible features were delivered in earlier commits within the same release cycle.

eli5.text: This release makes it easier to invite friends, gives you more control over ads, and smooths out the buying and onboarding experience. Key highlights: a new 'refer-friends' command (with '/referral' still working as an alias) lets you generate a personal referral link to share with friends directly from the app; the credits-buying screen now offers simple fixed dollar amounts instead of a custom input, removing confusion; turning off ads is now possible right from the ad banner with an info panel that explains what the ad supports; and the web onboarding flow was rewritten to be shorter and clearer, removing extra emoji and redundant text. Upgrading means faster, cleaner sign-up, an easier way to earn rewards by sharing the service, simpler credit top-ups, and a one-click way to hide ads with an explanation of why they exist.
